stages.label: Repair needs arrive
stages.narrative: Named projects request specific cable families, quantities, priorities, and deadlines.

stages.label: Stock becomes contested
stages.narrative: Compatibility, depot reserves, damaged reels, and daily vehicle capacity constrain feasible allocations.

stages.label: Transfers move
stages.narrative: Metered cable leaves an identified reel, travels to a project, and advances completion only when it arrives.

stages.label: Policies settle
stages.narrative: Cheapest, fastest-restoration, and fairness-first branches close with matching reel, transfer, project, and cost receipts.

seeds.label: Neighborhood backbone shortage
seeds.description: Copper-heavy repair demand competes for constrained depot reels during a modeled road closure.
seeds.missionText: Run the governed neighborhood cable-restoration crisis and compare allocation policies.

seeds.label: Fiber restoration
seeds.description: Hospital and transit projects compete for OS2 and OM4 stock with incompatible copper remaining nearby.
seeds.missionText: Run the governed fiber-restoration crisis and explain each allocation.

seeds.label: Emergency restoration
seeds.description: Critical projects receive short deadlines and expose the cost of reserve and transfer-capacity policies.
seeds.missionText: Run the governed emergency-restoration crisis and compare time to completion.

seeds.label: Borough fairness conflict
seeds.description: Two critical sites contest the same cable family so cheapest and fairness-first policies diverge.
seeds.missionText: Run the governed fairness conflict and compare who remains short.
